subject: SCIENCE
title: Sound Starts with Vibrations
objective: Relate sound to vibration and practice hearing safety.
introduction: Milo plucks a string and sees it shake before he hears sound. What is vibrating, and how can Maxine protect her hearing?

vocabulary.definition: Something you hear when vibrations travel through a material to your ears.
Using your ears to notice vibrations and sounds.
A quick back-and-forth movement that can make sound.

items.prompt: Maxine plucks a string and turns on a speaker. Which statement about sound is true?

options.text: Sound travels through perfect empty space
Loudness and pitch are the same
Sound begins with vibration and travels through a medium.
Sound can only travel through metal.

items.explanation: Sound starts when something vibrates and travels through air or another material. It cannot cross a perfect vacuum, and loudness and pitch describe different features.

items.prompt: Milo plucks a guitar string and watches it move. Which example shows how sound begins?
items.explanation: Plucking makes the string shake back and forth, and that vibration makes sound. A still string, quiet room, or color is not the sound source.

items.prompt: Milo reads four sound claims. Which one is NOT true?
items.explanation: Sound needs matter such as air to carry vibrations, so it cannot travel through a perfect vacuum. Strings and speaker cones vibrate to make sound.

items.prompt: A learner plucks a string and feels it shake. What starts the sound?
items.explanation: The string moves back and forth quickly, and that vibration starts the sound. Color, shadow, and stillness do not make the string vibrate.

items.prompt: Maxine uses headphones for music. Which choice helps protect her hearing?

options.text: Press the speaker against an ear
Listen for hours without a break

items.explanation: Lower volume is gentler on ears, and taking breaks also helps. Maximum volume and pressing speakers close can damage hearing.
